name: MagicPost
tagline: AI tool that drafts social posts from a prompt or topic and helps you queue them for publishing.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The interesting half of this product is a prompt template plus an LLM call, and a coding agent will reproduce that in an afternoon, including tone presets, hook variants, and a thread splitter. The boring half is publishing, and that is where it stops being fun: LinkedIn and Instagram both want app review, X charges for write access, and every token refresh is a chance for your queue to silently die. A local drafting tool that generates posts and puts them on your clipboard is genuinely a one-sitting build and covers most of the daily value. Actual scheduled auto-posting across multiple networks is a weekend of OAuth plumbing followed by ongoing maintenance you did not sign up for. So: yes to the writing, kinda to the posting.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that turns a topic or rough note into platform-specific post drafts with tone and length controls, stores them in a queue, and copies or posts them one at a time.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic)
Node 20 and a local machine or cheap VPS
Developer apps and OAuth credentials for any network you actually want to auto-post to
Tolerance for re-authorizing tokens when they expire
whatYouLose: Pre-approved platform apps, so you inherit the API review and rate limit pain yourself
A scheduler that runs when your laptop is closed, unless you deploy and babysit it
Prompt tuning that someone else already iterated on across thousands of posts
Analytics on what actually performed, which is the part that makes a content tool worth paying for
Mobile access for posting from a phone queue
moatNotes: The moat is not the AI, it is the approved developer apps and the token refresh logic nobody wants to own.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because writing the draft was never the expensive part. Paying a few dollars a month means someone else keeps the LinkedIn app in good standing, refreshes the tokens, retries the failed posts, and runs the cron at 9am while you are asleep. A self-hosted version works great for two months and then quietly stops publishing on a Tuesday, and you find out three weeks later.
notes: Build the drafting half locally, and only wire up publishing for the one network you actually post to.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI social post studio. No accounts, no telemetry, no cloud database.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/posts.db, schema created on boot
- OpenAI SDK, model and key read from .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_MODEL)
- Runs with `npm run dev` on port 3000 and nothing else

Core features:
1. A composer page: paste a rough note, link, or topic. Pick target platform (x, linkedin, instagram-caption), tone (plain, punchy, technical, warm), and length.
2. On generate, call the LLM and return 3 distinct drafts, each with a separate hook line and body. Show them side by side.
3. Per-platform rules enforced in the prompt and validated in code: X 280 chars per post with auto thread splitting, LinkedIn 3000 chars with line breaks preserved, Instagram caption 2200 chars with a hashtag block.
4. Save any draft to a queue table with status (idea, ready, posted), a scheduled_at datetime, and free text notes.
5. Queue page: list by date, inline edit, character counter, one click "copy to clipboard", one click mark as posted.
6. A reusable prompt library: user-editable system prompts stored in the DB, seeded with 4 defaults, selectable in the composer.
7. Import a writing sample file (.txt or .md) and include it in the prompt as a style reference. Store samples in the DB.
8. Export the whole queue to JSON and to a folder of markdown files.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build:
- OAuth, auto-publishing, or any platform write API
- Image generation, carousels, or video
- Analytics, multi-user, billing, hosted deploy

Requirements:
- Seed 5 example queue rows so the UI is not empty on first run
- .env.example committed, .env and ./data gitignored
- Handle a missing API key with a clear in-app message, not a crash
- README with setup in under 10 lines and an honest note that scheduling here only reminds, it does not post
